issues.title: Missing ConfigureAwait(false) on Task.Yield
issues.description: The rule requires all await expressions in library code (non-test, non-sample projects) to use .ConfigureAwait(false) to avoid capturing the synchronization context, but the await Task.Yield() expression at line 291 omits it.
issues.rule_name: Async Methods Must Use ConfigureAwait(false) in Library Code

issues.title: Logout validation incorrectly rejects valid logout requests when HistoryEntryState is null
issues.description: The sign-out validation logic was modified to remove the null check for Navigation.HistoryEntryState before calling ValidateSignOutRequestState(). This causes ValidateSignOutRequestState() to return false when HistoryEntryState is null (since GetCachedNavigationState() returns null), which incorrectly redirects users to the logout failure page even for legitimate logout operations. The original code correctly allowed logout when HistoryEntryState is null by using the condition 'HistoryEntryState != null && !ValidateSignOutRequestState()', which only validated if state existed. This breaks backward compatibility with logout flows that don't use history state.

issues.title: Missing null check for InteractiveRequestUrl causes potential null reference in navigation
issues.description: The Redirect() method condition was changed from checking both InteractionOptions and InteractiveRequestUrl to only checking InteractionOptions. This creates a bug where if InteractionOptions is not null but InteractiveRequestUrl is null, the code will call NavigateToLogin with a null URL parameter at line 40. The NavigateToLogin method expects a non-null URL, so this will cause a null reference exception or navigation failure. The original PR properly validated both properties before choosing the navigation method.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #62755 - [Blazor] Remove obsolete APIs from Components

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes a batch of previously obsolete Blazor APIs across Components, Forms, Web, WebAssembly and WebAssembly.Authentication: `Router.PreferExactMatches`, `AddDataAnnotationsValidation`, the no-IServiceProvider `EnableDataAnnotationsValidation` overload, `RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions`, the `WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions` class, the `WebRenderer.RendererId` init accessor, `JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged(string, bool)`, `SignOutSessionStateManager`, and several `AccessTokenResult`/`RemoteAuthenticationService` obsolete members. Each removal is matched by `*REMOVED*` lines in the Unshipped PublicAPI files, and I grepped the repo and found no lingering references to the removed types.

The mechanical deletions look correct. The risk is concentrated in three behavioral edits that go beyond deletion: the logout validation rewrite in `RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut`, the `AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect` change that drops the null guard and the legacy fallback, and an unexplained `Task.Yield()` added to the logout path. The logout change also contradicts the PR description, and the test removed alongside it leaves the new branch uncovered.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The API deletions are sound, but the logout rewrite changes behavior in a way the PR description says it does not, and the redirect change may produce a nullable warning (likely a build break under warnings-as-errors) and a runtime ArgumentNullException. These should be resolved or explicitly justified before merge. The InternalCalls removal needs confirmation from the runtime side.

architecture.overview:
In the WebAssembly authentication stack, `RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore` is the component that handles `/authentication/logout` callbacks. It validates the logout request, calls `RemoteAuthenticationService.SignOutAsync`, and navigates to a success or failure path. Token acquisition goes through `RemoteAuthenticationService.RequestAccessToken`, which returns an `AccessTokenResult`. When that result requires interaction, `AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect()` uses the result's `InteractiveRequestUrl` and `InteractionOptions` to navigate to the login page. Before this PR there were two parallel logout-validation mechanisms: the `HistoryEntryState` set by `NavigateToLogout`, and a legacy session-storage flag managed by `SignOutSessionStateManager`.

The PR removes the legacy session-storage path and every obsolete overload that routed through it. Logout validation now depends only on `HistoryEntryState`. Token redirects now depend only on `InteractiveRequestUrl` and `InteractionOptions`. The other removals are self-contained deletions in Components, Forms and Web, with matching PublicAPI `*REMOVED*` records.
steps: Entry point: `RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut` runs on the logout path. Before this PR it checked `HistoryEntryState`, and when that was null it fell back to `SignOutSessionStateManager` session storage. After this PR it checks only `ValidateSignOutRequestState()`, which returns false whenever `HistoryEntryState` is null.

Token path: `RemoteAuthenticationService.RequestAccessToken` builds an `AccessTokenResult` with the URL and options set together, using the 4-argument constructor. `AccessTokenResult.RedirectUrl` and the 3-argument obsolete constructor are removed.

Redirect path: `AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect()` now branches on `InteractionOptions` alone. The obsolete `RedirectUrl` fallback is gone, and the else branch navigates to `InteractiveRequestUrl!` without a null check.

Deletions: `RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions`, `WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions`, `WebRenderer.RendererId.init`, `Router.PreferExactMatches`, `EnableDataAnnotationsValidation(EditContext)`, `AddDataAnnotationsValidation`, the `RemoteAuthenticationService` constructor without a logger, and `JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged(string, bool)`. Each is removed along with its PublicAPI entry.
Interop: `InternalCalls.InvokeJS` is removed. Its comment says the name must match a Mono `driver.c` entry for backcompat, so this deletion needs a runtime-side check.
Tests: the logout test for an invalid sign-out state is removed, along with the `TestSignOutSessionStateManager` helper. No test is added for the new null-state behavior.

findings.title: Logout now rejects any request without HistoryEntryState, contradicting the PR description
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` (around lines 281-286) now rejects every logout whose `Navigation.HistoryEntryState` is null, because `ValidateSignOutRequestState()` returns false when there is no cached state. The PR description says null state should be handled and only an existing-but-invalid state should fail. Decide which behavior is intended. If the null case should pass, restore a guard that only fails when the state is non-null and invalid. If null should fail, update the PR description and add a test asserting the redirect to `LogOutFailedPath`, following the style of the test that was removed from `RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs`.

findings.title: AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect passes a nullable URL and drops the null guard
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/Services/AccessTokenNotAvailableException.cs`, `Redirect()` (lines 38-46) now checks only `_tokenResult.InteractionOptions`. It passes `InteractiveRequestUrl`, which is `string?`, to `NavigateToLogin`, which takes a non-null string, and it calls `NavigateTo(InteractiveRequestUrl!)` in the else branch. Restore a null check on `InteractiveRequestUrl` before each navigation call, so that a null URL cannot reach `NavigationManager` and the nullable flow analysis stays clean. Keep the existing behavior for the `InteractionOptions` branch. Confirm the project builds with warnings as errors.

findings.title: Unexplained Task.Yield() added to the logout path with a misleading comment
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` has an `await Task.Yield();` at about line 291 with the comment "Ensure we're authenticated before proceeding with sign-out." That comment does not match the code, since the yield does not check authentication. Either remove the yield if nothing depends on it, or keep it and replace the comment with the actual reason, such as the race or ordering issue it prevents. Verify with the existing `RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests` that the logout flow still passes.

findings.title: Removed Mono-facing InvokeJS extern without confirming runtime dependency
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/JSInterop/src/InternalCalls.cs`, the `InvokeJS` extern that the comment says must match an entry in Mono's `driver.c` was removed. Confirm with the WebAssembly runtime owners that the runtime no longer looks up this symbol by name, including for mixed-version runtime packs. If it still does, restore the extern with its `[Obsolete]` attribute and the comment. If not, note the verification in the PR description so the removal is justified.

findings.title: Removed logout test leaves the null-state path with no coverage
findings.body:
The test `AuthenticationManager_Logout_RedirectsToFailureOnInvalidSignOutState` is deleted, along with its `TestSignOutSessionStateManager` helper. The test covered the "logout not initiated from within the page" redirect. No replacement test covers the post-change behavior, which is the null-`HistoryEntryState` case that now always fails. So the one behavior this PR changed in logout validation has no test.

::diff{file="src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs" lines="370-373"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs`, the logout test for an invalid sign-out state was deleted around line 373. Add back a test that drives `LogOut` with no `HistoryEntryState` and asserts the navigation goes to `logout-failed` with the message "The logout was not initiated from within the page." This covers the null-state behavior that `ProcessLogOut` now enforces. Follow the structure of the nearby `NavigatesToLogoutFailureOnError` test.

findings.title: Obsolete API removals are complete and consistently recorded
findings.body:
The PublicAPI changes are consistent. Each removed symbol has a `*REMOVED*` line in the Unshipped file for its project, the Shipped files are untouched, and the `~` marker on `NotifyLocationChanged` matches the obsolete-marker convention used in the existing Shipped files. I grepped the repo for the removed types and members (`PreferExactMatches`, `AddDataAnnotationsValidation`, `RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions`, `WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions`, `SignOutSessionStateManager`, `NotifyLocationChanged`, and `RedirectUrl`) and found no remaining references in .cs or .razor code.

The `EnableDataAnnotationsValidation(EditContext, IServiceProvider)` overload stays in place, so the supported path remains available.
